summary: Pt/SnO2 core–shell nanowires were synthesized using thermal evaporation of SnO2 nanowires followed by atomic layer deposition (ALD) of Pt. The Pt shell significantly enhanced the gas and photon-sensing properties of the nanowires.
evidence: The Pt /SnO2 core–shell nanowires exhibit a much higher gas sensitivity of /H1101122.0 to 500 ppm ethanol vapor, which obviously increases to 15.6 times that of pristine SnO2 nanowires, and both the gas and photoresponse and recovery time of Pt /SnO2 core–shell nanowires are much smaller than that of pristine SnO 2 nanowires. During ALD, the container for MeCpPtMe3 was kept at 45°C, providing a steady-state flux of MeCpPtMe3 at a constant pressure of 0.308 Torr to the reactor. After the preparation of SnO2 nanowires, Pt nanofilms were deposited on the nanowire surface to form Pt /SnO2 core–shell nanowires by ALD of Pt after 250 reaction cycles using alternating exposures to MeCpPtMe3 and oxygen at 250°C.
